title: Do LLM Routers Actually Route? Quick answer: Not much!
gist: AutoBench's pre-registered Router Benchmark scored seven commercial and open-source LLM routers (17 settings) on 252 open-ended prompts across 20 models and found none beats always calling one mid-priced model (GPT-5.6 Luna) on quality and cost together. Many routers are effectively constants with a knob, and independent routers rarely agree on the model to pick.

themes.theme: Headline result: routers fail the bar

insights.claim: None of seven commercial and open-source LLM routers, across 17 settings, beats always calling one mid-priced model (GPT-5.6 Luna) on quality and cost together, and in 10,000 bootstrap resamples no setting ever did.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Paying for a router is hard to justify versus a static mid-tier model; ask vendors for evidence against that baseline.
insights.quote: None of them beats always calling one mid-priced model on quality and cost together.

insights.claim: Always calling GPT-5.6 Luna scores 85.3% Delta-Hit at $0.0043 per question, most of the top model's quality at about 5% of its bill, with no router required.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Mid-tier models capture most of the quality at a fraction of the cost, which pressures premium-model and router pricing.

insights.claim: The Autobench Router Index at a locked cost weight of 0.2 ranks Always-Luna first, and no commercial router has positive lift against it.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: A single joint quality-cost metric favors static mid-tier policies over routing today.
insights.locator: One number: the Autobench Router Index

insights.claim: A per-prompt oracle that picks the cheapest model still inside the quality bar scores 100% Delta-Hit at $0.0018 per question, versus 87.5% at $0.079 for always calling the top model GPT-5.6 Sol.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: A perfect router could add about 12 quality points while cutting cost about 98%, so the opportunity is real but uncaptured.
insights.quote: In other words, the perfect router offers the potential to gain about 12 points in quality against the best static model, while costing about 98% less.

insights.claim: The random-pick baseline scores 64.7% Delta-Hit at $0.0115, and because the board is packed near the top of the scale a coin flip already looks decent.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Read router quality claims against the random line, not against 100%.
insights.locator: How the AutoBench Router Benchmark works

insights.claim: Five of the 17 router settings send at least 90% of prompts to a single model, so their quality score is just that model's score, and a quality knob often only changes which constant you get.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Request top-model share at every knob setting before buying a router.
insights.locator: Most routers are constants with a knob

insights.claim: Not Diamond's cost-quality knob is a cliff: quality holds through knob 4 (80.3% at $0.060) but at knob 5 cost falls about 64-fold and quality drops to 46.6%, below random; at knob 0 it names Sol on every prompt.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: A cost-quality dial without a usable middle is not a real trade-off curve.

insights.claim: OpenRouter Auto's low tier sends 98% of prompts to one cheap model and lands on the random line (65.7%), and its high and max tiers score alike at 79.1% and 78.3% while max costs more.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: OpenRouter Auto behaves as a spend tier rather than a route.

insights.claim: Orca's cheapest and balanced strategies send 99-100% of prompts to one open model and score 39.3%, worse than random, while its quality strategy sends nearly everything to a cheap model (65.7%).
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Strategy names do not guarantee distinct routing behavior.

insights.claim: Azure Model Router's quality option scores 85.3% at $0.065, matching Always-Luna's quality at about fifteen times the price within a 3-of-20 catalog.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler-bundled routers may add cost without adding quality; test against a static baseline.
insights.quote: Luna’s quality at fifteen times the price

insights.claim: NadirClaw sent most prompts to Sol and scored 70.3% at $0.051 (close to random), Brick scored 63.9% at $0.0031 on the random line, and a FrugalGPT-style cascade scored 60.9%, below random.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Classifier-, capability-map- and cascade-based routers all failed to beat the static baseline here; note Brick was run on models it was not tuned for.

insights.claim: Across 59 cross-vendor router pairs the median same-pick rate is 0 and 57.6% of pairs are exactly 0, indicating there is no discoverable right model per prompt that independent routers converge on.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: If routers cannot agree, routing quality claims are weak evidence; demand per-workload validation.

insights.claim: High agreement arises from shared collapse: Orca quality and OpenRouter Auto low tier agree on 248 of 252 prompts because both default to the same cheap flash model.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger

insights.claim: ARB uses 252 long, open-ended prompts across ten domains and five difficulty levels, answered once by 20 models and scored by a committee of ten LLM judges, with real billed cost stored beside each score; routers are graded by looking up the model they pick.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Lookup-based grading makes testing a new router cheap, so expect more router audits.
insights.locator: How the AutoBench Router Benchmark works

insights.claim: Rules were locked on 29 August 2026 before any router was called (calls 30 Aug-1 Sep), and the blog says a new router can be scored by a lookup while adding questions is the expensive step.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Pre-registration increases credibility, but AutoBench sells evaluation and offers custom router benchmarks, so a commercial interest exists.

insights.claim: On short multiple-choice boards a cheap model is often already the best choice, so a router that always names it can look strong; long open-ended prompts that cost 10-100x more to answer are the regime a router is sold into.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: Prior router leaderboards on short items may overstate router value for enterprise prompts.

insights.claim: Before buying a router, check the static-policy baseline, top-model share at every knob, whether the knob has a middle, whether independent routers agree on your prompts, and which board the claim was measured on.
insights.speaker: Peter Kruger
insights.so_what: A usable due-diligence checklist for LLM-gateway procurement.
insights.quote: it is a knob in front of a constant
